messages.author: 29ce8550baceaeb0
messages.subject: Mixed data - parameter simplex
parts:
Quick question - 

Let's say I have the first 4 values of a six-dimensional simplex, and I want to a) make estimates of alpha below, and b) generate predictions (par1 .. par3), which are parameters of the model. The restriction of course is that the parameters + data = 1. 

[data1, data2, data3, data4, par1, par2, par3]' ~ dirichlet(alpha)

Any suggestions on how to implement this? 

Currently, I'm building the simplex in the transformed parameters block, then calculating the log absolute determinant of the inverse transform (I think?). Is this just the log of the second expression on p487 of the 2.11 manual? To my mind, the model would then be something like

model {
// prior on alpha

// Expression which I suppose gives some structure to par1...par3?
target += my_log_abs_jac_inv_trans_calculated_elsewher;

//likelihood
my_simplex ~ dirichlet(alpha);

}

Does that seem right? I'm doing this at the moment and it's not working. So I'm trying to work out whether my approach to implementing is wrong, or whether I'm calculating the wrong log abs jac... 

Cheers, 
Jim

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixed data - parameter simplex
parts:
Hmm... it seems like you should have something like:

data {
  vector[4] x;
}
parameters {
  simplex[2] alpha;
}
transformed parameters {
  simplex[6] beta;
  beta[1:4] = x;
  beta[5] = alpha[1] / (1 - sum(x));
  beta[6] = alpha[2] / (1 - sum(x));
}

Since x is data, I don't think you need a Jacobian here. That's beta[5] and beta[6] are just alpha[1] and alpha[2] divided by a constant.

Does that make sense?

(Of course, you could simplify in this case by using real<lower = 0, upper = 1> alpha and using alpha and (1 - alpha)).


Daniel

Now my problem is a bit more difficult. My data actually look more like

Y = 

[.4, .2, NA, NA;
 .5, .1, .1, NA;
 .2, NA, NA, NA]

where each row is a simplex by design, but where different rows have different
number of missing rows (that will be imputed using the parameters above). 
Each row has at least one missing value (to be clear, I'm not giving Stan missing 
values; I'm giving it an accompanying position matrix for the missing observations. 

So I'm not sure I can use the elegant solution above. 

Cheers, 
Jim

Daniel

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Mixed data - parameter simplex
parts:
You just need to build up each row of Y separately.
There's no good way to generalize here because each simplex
has to be declared separately to get the size right.

You could pass in the data as a matrix as long as you
don't mind some unused values, but you'd need something
else like

int row_data_sizes[M]; // num data elements in row m

to say how many rows each has, and given that each simplex
is separate, you'd want to break the build-up into a function
to avoid code duplication.

- Bob

>>>> model {

>>>>

>>>>
>>>> }
>>>>
>>>> Does that seem right? I'm doing this at the moment and it's not working. So I'm trying to work out whether my approach to implementing is wrong, or whether I'm calculating the wrong log abs jac...
>>>>
>>>> Cheers,
>>>> Jim
